text:
maria: Quick follow-up after the attention RFC — ran our nightly perf sweep and FA v3 is ~8-12% slower than v2 on medium sequences (512/768) for small batches. Can we triage?
ajay: ugh. which model/config? any padding or workspace fragmentation in the traces?
sophia: looks like the run was on gpt-like-1.3B, batch=4, seq=512, quant=fp16. No artificial padding, but we do see multiple small allocations in the CUDA logs.
ryan: can you paste the exact bench command? also include kernel selection flags.
maria: here: `./bench_attn --model gpt-1.3b --batch 4 --seq 512 --kernel flashattn_v3 --quant fp16 --trace=mini`
ajay: thanks. initial hypothesis: v3's tiling heuristics pick a kernel variant that favors long streams; for mid-seq + small batch it might fall back to a slower path due to workspace sizing.
sophia: I noticed in telemetry that v3 requests are hitting a tiny workspace (reserve < 2MB) and then doing repeated reallocs. That explains fragmentation costs.
ryan: is that from our allocator or from FA3's internal workspace API?
maria: traces show repeated calls to `fa::alloc_workspace` interspersed with kernel launches. allocator logs have: `alloc 1.9MB -> ok`, `alloc 3.2MB -> cudaMalloc` a lot.
ajay: ok two things to check: 1) our workspace pooling config (default pool slab size) 2) the kernel_size heuristic mapping in v3. If v3 expects larger contiguous buffer it may do more cudaMallocs for intermediate tiling.
sophia: can we try forcing v3 to use the v2-like kernel for those shapes using env var? I can run a quick A/B.
ryan: use `ATTN_KERNEL_PREFER=flashattn_v2` in the runner. also set `POOL_SLAB=8MB` to see if pooling fixes it.
maria: running now. dev-bot: CI bench job 1952456799 finished — baseline (v2): mean latency 42.1ms, p95 55.3ms.
(5m later)
maria: test with POOL_SLAB=8MB + v3 preferred: mean 40.8ms, p95 52.9ms. Better but still noisy.
ajay: so pooling helps. that supports the fragmentation hypothesis. Remaining delta could be kernel math differences or extra indexing overhead in v3's tile loops.
sophia: I added a tiny microprobe in the runtime to emit `kernel_choice` tag and workspace bytes. sample trace: `kernel_choice=FA3_TILED_32, workspace=6.4MB, launch_ms=0.84`. For v2 earlier we had `FA2_FUSED` workspace=2.1MB launch_ms=0.72.
ryan: interesting — FA3_TILED_32 has more launch overhead but may scale better at large seq. For our production SLOs (latency-sensitive small batches) the opt should prefer FA2_FUSED. We need a policy layer to map shape->kernel with perf-weighted scores.
ajay: agreed. short-term: add a config override mapping (shape->preferred_kernel) and route warm-up traffic. Long-term: integrate offline perf model into kernel selector.
maria: also want to flag potential compaction in FA3: we saw a memcpy step when seq<768 that doesn't exist in v2. Could be an alignment pad for vectorized ops.
sophia: filed GH issue: redwood/flashattn-adapter#412 — includes perf traces and sample logs.
ryan: action items: (1) Sophia — run full matrix (batches 1..8, seq 128,256,512,768) with pool slab 4/8/16MB and attach traces. (2) Ajay — add shape->kernel override to runtime config and a rollout flag. (3) Maria — coordinate with FA upstream on the memcpy pad behavior and share logs.
maria: ack. tagging @here in eng-runtime and will open a short RFC patch for the override API. :thumbsup:
dev-bot: deploy-notify: feature/attn-override pushed to canary cluster (no traffic) at 1952456950.
ryan: once we have the override and perf model, we can gate v3 default to long-seq heavy workloads and keep v2 as fallback for latency-critical routes.
ajay: one more note — quantization interacts with kernel selection. fp16 seemed fine but int8 fallback paths triggered extra transforms. Sophia include quant runs too.
sophia: will do. posting results as separate threads to avoid noise.
maria: thanks all — close loop on this by EOD tomorrow.
